text:
incidentbot: @oncall P1: widespread signing failures detected - external KMS (gcp-kms) returning 5xx/504 for key lookup/sign calls. Auto-mitigation triggered: fallback disabled pending human review. Paging @sara (oncall) :rotating_light:

incidentbot: affected services: agent-startup, request-signing. Impact: new Dedicated node startups failing; ~8-12% request signing errors seen in prod across us-west2 and eu-central1.

sara (oncall): seeing it, joining. Thanks for the page. what's the error surface?

raj (sre): logs show repeated 502/504 from kms.googleapis.com for cryptoKeys/cryptoKeyVersions: 
```
WARN sign_request - 2026-03-15T15:34:10Z - upstream error: 504 Gateway Timeout from kms.googleapis.com - retried 2x
ERROR node_startup - 2026-03-15T15:35:02Z - failed to fetch key version metadata: context deadline exceeded
```

raj (sre): also seeing increased latency on initial key fetch (200ms -> 2.5s) before the 5xx storm.

mike (infra): confirm on our side: healthchecks show spike in signer latency, autoscaler is spinning up more Dedicated workers which then fail at init because signing fails. This is amplifying load.

lexi (support): any customer-facing impact yet? I have 3 support tickets referencing failed requests around 15:30 UTC. One customer reported 502 when calling Redwood API for model inference.

sara (oncall): ok triage plan: 1) throttle autoscaler to stop spiraling 2) enable local cached-signing fallback for existing nodes 3) open cloud provider ticket and get region-level status 4) notify CS + docs. Doing 1 now.

mike (infra): throttling autoscaler to 20% ramp, applying patch: `kubectl -n redwood patch hpa signer-workers --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":10}}'` — applied.

sara (oncall): enabling cached-signing fallback for nodes already running (hotfix toggle): `POST /admin/feature-toggle` body `{ "cached_signing_fallback": "on" }` — pushed. This will allow currently running agents to use cached key material for up to 30m.

raj (sre): pushing rollover to fallback added ~40% reduction in immediate error rate. Confirming from metrics: signing error rate dropped from 11% -> 6% in 5m.

incidentbot: created incident-2076543210 in the tracker, severity P1.

lexi (support): messaging draft for customers: "We're investigating intermittent signing failures affecting some requests in us-west2 and eu-central1; we have temporary mitigations in place. We'll post updates every 30 minutes." OK to send?

sara (oncall): yes send now.

mike (infra): cloud-support-bot: opened ticket with GCP. Case ID GC-8923412. Provider response: "We are seeing increased error ratio on KMS control plane in us-west2. Mitigation in progress, estimated 2-3h."

cloud-support-bot: GCP status link: https://status.cloud.google.com/incident/kms/2026-03-15 - "Investigating - degraded performance for KMS in US-WEST2"

raj (sre): potential mitigations while provider works: 1) route signing traffic to eu-central1/secondary KMS key replicas (requires key policy/replica config) 2) extend cached signing TTL to 2h for critical flows 3) temporary in-memory signing with customer consent (security review). Thoughts?

sara (oncall): we can't do in-memory signing for customer keys without legal/crypto sign-off. Option (1) is feasible for our service keys if replicas exist - checking key replication config now.

mike (infra): checked: service-master-key is multi-region and has active replica in europe-west1. There's an IAM restriction on the worker nodes' SA for that replica - need a short auth tweak.

raj (sre): I can push an allowlist change for the worker SA on the replica for a 3h window. Will do a targeted rollout to the signing-service only.

sara (oncall): do it, but let's stage: change IAM, then test on canary signer instance with a manual call.

raj (sre): IAM change applied to allow kms.cryptoSign on `projects/xyz/locations/europe-west1/keyRings/rdw/cryptoKeys/service-master-key` for `signer-worker-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.

mike (infra): initiating canary sign call: `gcloud kms keys versions asymmetric-sign ...` -> response OK from european replica, sign time ~120ms.

raj (sre): canary success. Rolling signer workers in us-west2 with new replica route config (gradual 10% batch). Rolling now.

lexi (support): updating customers: added note that we are routing signing to EU replica where possible and that some startups may still fail briefly during the rollout.

incidentbot: paging @oncall for handoff in 45 minutes.

sara (oncall): handing off in 45m to @raj for night watch. I'll stay on for 10m to confirm stability; after that @raj you own mitigation until cloud confirms full recovery.

raj (sre): acknowledged. I'll keep monitoring key error rate, latency, and autoscaler behavior. Setting alert thresholds lower to detect regression.

mike (infra): note: autoscaler kept at fixed min replicas to avoid re-amplification. Recommend re-enable gradual scaling once sign error <1% for 15m.

sara (oncall): quick customer-impact summary for post: "Impact: intermittent signing failures caused delayed node startups and ~8-12% request failures for affected regions. Mitigation: temporary cached-signing fallback and cross-region replica routing; autoscaler throttled to prevent amplification. Provider (GCP) investigating KMS control plane; ticket GC-8923412. Next steps: monitor, coordinate with provider, prepare postmortem."

lexi (support): creating the customer incident update thread now and linking GC-8923412. I'll attach logs and sample request ids.

cloud-support-bot: GCP update (15:58 UTC): "Mitigation in progress; traffic reroutes and control plane fixes being applied. No ETA yet."

raj (sre): metrics check at 16:05 UTC: signing error rate 0.9% (down from 11%), startup failure rate back to baseline. I'll take the watch.

sara (oncall): thanks team. Handoff to @raj. I'll update the oncall schedule and mark myself OOO for the next shift.

raj (sre): taking over. Will post a status at +30m and escalate if error rate creeps above 2%.

incidentbot: note: remember postmortem requirement for P1 incidents. Assigned to sara and raj.

lexi (support): logging the impacted customers: cust-A, cust-B, cust-C. CS will follow up for any contractual impact.

mike (infra): follow-ups: 1) add circuit-breaker to autoscaler to prevent spikes, 2) improve signer client to prefer cached keys + async refresh to reduce control plane pressure, 3) add runbook step for cross-region replica failover. I'll create infra tickets.

raj (sre): adding runbook entry now. Also scheduling a retrospective with security and legal for the in-memory signing discussion if ever needed.

sara (oncall): all good. leaving thread. good job everyone :thumbsup:
